question: Under the Mental Healthcare Act 2017 (India), a person with mental illness may make a legally valid advance directive specifying the treatments they wish to receive or refuse during a future mental health crisis.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Incorrect. The MHCA 2017 does allow advance directives. Under Section 5, a person with mental illness can make a written document specifying their treatment preferences and a nominated representative — this is legally binding on treating clinicians within specified limits.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Section 5 of the MHCA 2017 explicitly grants every person with mental illness the right to make an advance directive (Nominated Representative and treatment preferences). This is a landmark provision recognising the autonomy and decision-making rights of persons with mental illness in India, even in anticipation of future incapacity.
